Use case: identity-preserve illustration-story. Create one new EIGHT-DIRECTION elevated-view sprite atlas of the EXACT SAME person as the reference. Reference is identity, clothing, flat-color style and azimuth layout; change camera elevation ONLY, not the outfit, hair, face, stride or character.
CRITICAL CAMERA CHANGE: Every one of the eight cells must be genuinely viewed from 30 DEGREES ABOVE THE HORIZON looking down at the person. Moderate high angle: clearly visible top of head, top planes of shoulders and shoes, slightly foreshortened torso and legs; all bodies appear gently shortened by the elevated camera. Keep the camera elevated for FRONT, BACK, and SIDE views alike. Orthographic-like long lens, no fisheye.
Layout: transparent PNG 1536x1024, invisible 4 columns x 2 rows grid, exactly one FULL BODY walker in every cell, eight total. Center each projection in its 384x512 cell, ample clear margins, never cut heads/feet. Do NOT stretch the high-angle body to fill a tall cell; retain natural perspective foreshortening.
Azimuth order left-to-right: top row front toward viewer 0, front-right three-quarter 45 (nose to screen RIGHT), right-facing profile 90, rear-right three-quarter 135. Bottom row back180, rear-left three-quarter225, left-facing profile270, front-left three-quarter315. At every azimuth the camera is still 30 degrees high. SAME midstride walking pose rotated in space.
